abstract: Williams' algorithmic method turns nontrivial algorithms estimating acceptance probabilities into circuit lower bounds, and the strongest known gate-count lower bounds for depth-two threshold circuits follow this route. For circuits $C(x)=f(\sum_{i=1}^{q}T_i(x))$ with an arbitrary symmetric top $f:\{0,\ldots,q\}\to\{0,1\}$ and linear threshold bottom gates $T_i$ on $h$ variables, a natural plan is to estimate a single modular character of the bottom-gate sum and recover $f$ by linearity. We show that this primitive is as hard as the general problem. Let $R=2^\ell$ be the least power of two larger than $q$ and $\omega=e^{2\pi i/R}$. In deterministic polynomial time we construct $M=q(R-1)+\ell R+(R/2)|\{t\in\mathbb Z_R:f(t)=0\}|\le 4q^2+2q\log_2(2q)=O(q^2)$ linear threshold functions $U_1,\ldots,U_M$ on $h+2\ell+1$ variables, appearing with unit coefficients in the character exponent (their internal threshold weights remain general), such that $\mathbb E\,\omega^{\sum_{j}U_j}=R^{-1}\Pr_x[C(x)=1]$. The compression comes from logarithmically many uniform selector variables, combining character orthogonality with exact cancellation of rejected top values. Conversely, the character expectation is a Fourier combination of $R$ residue probabilities, each a symmetric-top counting query, so the primitives are polynomially interreducible when $R$ and $M$ are polynomially bounded. Estimating the acceptance probability within $\varepsilon$ requires the character expectation within $\varepsilon/R$, and in the reverse direction accuracy $\varepsilon/R$ per residue suffices. Deterministic algorithms transfer to deterministic algorithms; randomized ones transfer with a union bound over at most $R$ queries. The character expectation is complex-valued and differs from the Boolean acceptance probability of a single $\mathrm{MOD}_R$ gate. The equivalence is polynomial and need not preserve a particular gate-size exponent or precision regime. The result is a representation theorem: it gives no new algorithm or circuit lower bound and makes no claim about characters with a fixed modulus.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Tightened the loose $O(\ell^2 R + R)$ gate bound in the abstract, Problem and contribution, and Theorem 1 to the closed form $\ell R$ for the $-as \pmod R$ block (derived from $\sum_{b+c<\ell} 2^{b+c} = (\ell-1)R + 1$ replicated gates plus $R-1$ constant-one LTFs $1[0 \ge 0]$ representing $-(\ell-1)R - 1 \equiv R-1 \pmod R$) and overall gate count $M = q(R-1) + \ell R + (R/2)|\{t \in \mathbb Z_R : f(t)=0\}| \le q(R-1) + \ell R + R^2/2 \le 4q^2 + 2q\log_2(2q) = O(q^2)$, with explicit $L_i(x)$ and $B_i$ definitions before Eq. (6).
- Quantified the gate-count exponent halving ($2^{h'} = 2R^2\cdot 2^h \le 8q^2\cdot 2^h$ versus $M = \Theta(q^2)$ reducing $M \le h^\alpha$ to $q = O(h^{\alpha/2})$) in Section 2.
- Added primary-source Theorem, Lemma, Corollary, and Definition citations for [1]-[7] and completed STOC/FOCS page numbers, DOIs, and arXiv/ECCC identifiers in the References; normalized the author line.
- Upgraded supp/verify_construction.py and supp/README.md to check the closed-form gate count $M$, the Section 2 residue-Fourier combination, and identity (1) over the integer cyclotomic quotient $\mathbb Z[\omega] \cong \mathbb Z[X]/(X^{R/2}+1)$ alongside the $10^{-9}$ floating-point check on 30 random instances ($h \le 4$, $q \le 7$), and added CONTENTS.sha256.
title: A Single Modular Character Is Complete for SYM∘LTF Counting
